title: Shadow application-send pressure classifier architecture
purpose: Measure whether connection-local send pressure can reliably distinguish the retained c16 cooperative opportunity from c32 saturation before allowing an adaptive planner to change runtime behavior.
design_summary: A small mutable classifier remains connection-local and behavior-neutral. When its diagnostic instruments are observed, stream-write inbox items retain their enqueue timestamp and the runtime feeds elapsed queue delay into an integer microsecond EWMA. Existing recovery flush boundaries feed a bounded distinct-stream count and whether the authorized datagram burst was exhausted. Consecutive evidence and separate entry/exit thresholds classify sparse, cooperative, or saturated pressure with hysteresis. Metrics expose observations and transitions, while the existing null planner, static selector, and send authority remain unchanged. A local orchestration script runs fixed-per-stream and fixed-total-byte cardinality shapes without embedding benchmark identities in production code.
alternatives_considered: Activate the four-datagram cooperative quantum immediately. Rejected because retained evidence improved c16 but regressed c32 by 32.2 percent.
Classify from queued-write count alone. Rejected because application-send recovery depth was usually one at both c16 and c32.
Classify from caller concurrency or stream-count settings. Rejected as benchmark overfitting and unavailable to the runtime in a general form.
Collect timestamps unconditionally. Deferred until the shadow evidence proves the signal; the diagnostic-only first slice avoids charging normal operation.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A transient high-delay or burst-limit sample must not change mode by itself.
Saturated mode must require sustained high queue delay and must require sustained relief before demotion.
Sparse mode must not be inferred while queue delay remains elevated.
Instrumentation must not add per-observation allocations or alter work-item ordering.
High-cardinality failures caused by generator exhaustion must remain stress-only and must not be reported as transport regressions.
data_and_state_considerations: The classifier stores one mode, one integer EWMA, and bounded consecutive-evidence counters per connection. It retains no stream IDs, payloads, work items, timestamps, or metric tag objects. Distinct IDs are counted into a fixed stack buffer only at an existing flush boundary and only while diagnostics observe the shadow metrics.
risks: Diagnostic instrumentation can perturb throughput; classification runs are attribution evidence and not performance claims.
Local thresholds may not generalize across hosts; fixed-work c1 through c1024 screens and later ProtocolLab confirmation are required before activation.
Queue delay can represent host saturation rather than connection saturation; mode evidence must be interpreted with target CPU and variance.
The available queue snapshot may undercount runnable streams; burst-limit frequency and delay are retained as independent signals.
